Riot is terrible at punishing players for bad behavior, trolling, afk'ing, and general fuckery. I've seen a few players complain about chat restrictions and low priority queue but clearly that's not cutting it. This is especially a problem in ranked where you have a bit higher stakes than just playing ARAM or teambuilder.

I understand there's a high number of players who get reported - but I've now played 12 games in a row over 2 days that had either a troll (build only boots and nothing else all game), and afker, a straight feeder, or someone who nonstop trash talked their own team. Every. Single. Game. One of them my team even won.

The punishments that are currently employed are not working to deter the behavior from happening, nor do you ever see anything about a "reformed" player beyond the occasional post. You look at the reporting system in other games that are smaller or less populated and wonder what the actual fuck excuse RIot has for not being better in this regard.

Seriously, you should get 1 free (verified) report and then be banned from that game mode for 24 hours on your 2nd one. Do it a 3rd and it's a week. 4th time is permaban from that game mode.

I doubt RIot will do this without significant pressure from the community, if then. They seem to have a "fuck you, it's our game" mentality - much the same way the admins at reddit have about their website.
The way Riot handles punishing players is a disgrace, to the point that there's no integrity of the ranked system.

I keep getting an error message on my MacBook Air that my startup disk is full. How do I fix this? What does this mean? Why do I keep getting it as a popup? Thanks in advance!
Error Message About Startup Disk Being Full.

It means that your harddrive is full! You may need to delete some files, clear out temp/cache files and/or move files to a storage drive like an external harddrive or thumbdrive.

You can follow these steps to see how much space is taken up.

  • Click on the Apple in the top left and select "About This Mac"
  • Click the "More Info" button
  • Click the "Storage" tab to view your storage overview
